licenseNote: Original genre-inspired worlds. Not licensed franchise canon.

worlds.name: The City Between Panels
worlds.premise: A metropolis where panels and continuity are physical.
worlds.conflict: A hero's tragedy is treated as mandatory.
worlds.mechanics: Panel transitions are traversable; retcons leave echoes; framing changes perception, not consent.

worlds.name: The Orchard of Moving Castles
worlds.genre: fairy tales and whimsical dark fantasy
worlds.premise: Moving houses and migrating forests make maps negotiable.
worlds.conflict: A guardian imprisons people in a protective labyrinth.
worlds.mechanics: Roads shift with choices; names make promises; protection has limits.

worlds.name: The Starship Commons
worlds.premise: Living ships carry diverse civilizations between stars.
worlds.conflict: A navigation intelligence hides dangerous destinations.
worlds.mechanics: Ships require resources; navigation is collective; intelligences can advise, not compel.
worlds.ethics: Risk must remain an informed choice.

worlds.name: The Department of Unfinished Lessons
worlds.premise: A sprawling administration audits dreams, memory and metaphysical cases.
worlds.conflict: Compulsory lessons have replaced meaningful consent.
worlds.mechanics: Each lesson has an audit trail; daemons are task agents, not inherently evil; appeals change rules.

worlds.name: Monsters After Midnight
worlds.premise: A coastal town has ghosts, vampires and other unusual residents.
worlds.conflict: A political institution profits from mutual fear.
worlds.mechanics: Folklore is unreliable; needs vary by species; accusations require evidence.

worlds.name: The Neon Afterimage
worlds.premise: Embodied and simulated people share a layered city.
worlds.conflict: A population seeks liberation from systems others rely on.
worlds.mechanics: Copies may fork without syncing; embodiment costs energy; identities are negotiated.

worlds.name: The Kingdom of Side Quests
worlds.premise: Quest mechanics structure a sword-and-sorcery kingdom.
worlds.conflict: Ordinary vital labor is scored as nonessential.
worlds.mechanics: Quest boards can change; leveling credits actions; magic uses resources.
worlds.ethics: No one is an NPC in their own life.

worlds.name: The Kaiju Garden
worlds.premise: Giant beings restore ruined ecosystems while cities fear them.
worlds.conflict: A defense industry suppresses ecological evidence.
worlds.mechanics: Migrations have ecological causes; mecha need maintenance and synchronization; giant actions reshape habitats.

worlds.name: The Gentle Apocalypse
worlds.premise: Communities thrive after the fall of extractive civilization.
worlds.conflict: Rediscovered machines may repeat the catastrophe.
worlds.mechanics: Energy and feedstock remain finite; local decisions control adoption; old systems have risks.

crossoverRules: One to three selected worlds, each retaining its own physics and social rules.
Declare the precise boundary that connects worlds, including what can cross it and at what cost.
Do not silently equate magic, superpowers, simulation, and technology.
A trope reference is a character's guess, not reliable world evidence.
Write without hints of unpublished future twists; do not claim private author knowledge.
spoilerPolicy: Only this public entry-tier catalog is sent to the model. No private author notes, upcoming chapters, or hidden continuity are available through this protocol.
